name: Rebekah
tagline: A shared workshop. Clear rooms. A human at the door.
description: Rebekah gives agent execution, local inference, portable skills and engineering evidence a reproducible, self-hosted home. Distinct services keep distinct responsibilities, with an authenticated gateway between the workshop and the outside world.
status: Executable bootstrap · not yet a production-ready distribution
motifCaption: A home for cooperation, without blurring the boundaries.

featuredPublication.label: The boundary problem / Brief 01
featuredPublication.imageAlt: Separate service rooms connect only through an authenticated gateway; the public page stays outside.

demonstration.label: The boundary desk / Illustrated cases
demonstration.title: The same request meets four different doors.
demonstration.description: Select a case to see how one request is treated at each boundary of the workshop. Paths and outcomes are the documented ones, not live probes.
demonstration.disclaimer: Presentation-only illustrations. No request is sent and no access is granted by this explorer.

cases.title: Inside the room: loopback directly
cases.description: A supervised service answers on its own loopback address.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: loopback is for the supervisor and the operator on the machine — not a public address.

cases.title: At the door: the authenticated gateway
cases.description: An allow-listed backend route with a valid bearer credential.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: the gateway checks first and forwards second; the client never handles backend credentials.

cases.title: No such room: unexposed backend
cases.conclusion: Illustration: what is not exposed does not exist as far as the network is concerned.

cases.title: No credential: unauthenticated request
cases.description: An allow-listed route without any bearer credential.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: authentication happens before any backend sees the request.

highlights.label: Reproducibility
highlights.title: A runtime you can rebuild
highlights.text: A Nix-built OCI image brings the core tools together. Image pins and container checks make changes deliberate.

highlights.label: Separation
highlights.title: Every service has its own room
highlights.text: Separate identities and state directories help contain privileges. Loopback services are reached through an authenticated, allow-listed gateway.

highlights.label: Choice
highlights.title: Governance is explicit
highlights.text: The public baseline works without Ephor. Enable the separate governed integration when its policy and oversight fit the work.

sections.title: Put the workshop together without inventing another source of truth.
paragraphs: Rebekah is RAGBAZ’s reproducible, self-hosted runtime. OpenCode handles agent sessions, Ollama provides local inference, Sylvae runs portable skills and WeftMark records engineering provenance and review. Nostoi supplies audit-chain tooling.
The runtime packages and connects those responsibilities. It does not replace the products’ ledgers, model decisions or human review. Each service retains a distinct identity and state directory.

This is an executable bootstrap with tested building blocks, not a production-ready distribution. The practical question is whether a particular deployment meets its stated boundaries and has been verified on the host you intend to use.

sections.title: Clear boundaries make cooperation possible.
paragraphs: Services bind to loopback. Remote access belongs through the authenticated gateway and its allow-listed routes. Runtime secrets are injected; they should not enter the image or Nix store.
OpenCode’s HTTP access is authenticated. Per-service privilege separation matters because an agent’s tools can affect files and processes; a friendly interface is not an isolation boundary.
Use a pinned image and verify it in a real container. A reproducible recipe, a passing package build and a healthy running service are related but different observations.

sections.title: Give human oversight an actual place to act.
paragraphs: Ephor—the project formerly known as KAGP, the Konsonans AI Governance Platform—is an explicit opt-in integration. The public baseline does not require its private source or policy service.
In a governed deployment, held actions and human decisions travel through authenticated oversight paths. The system must not confuse an agent’s own explanation with permission to approve itself.

WeftMark remains responsible for engineering readiness. Ephor supplies governance judgments and audit references. A governance decision, a signature and a passing test should never be collapsed into one reassuring label.

sections.title: Self-hosting is a choice about agency, not a promise of innocence.
paragraphs: Local control can help a team understand where its data and work live, reduce dependence on one vendor and operate within its own resource constraints. It also creates duties: maintenance, backups, access control and careful handling of credentials.

RAGBAZ wants technology to support flourishing rather than anxiety or coercion. A legible workshop gives people room to question a result, stop a risky action and cooperate across different tools and skills.

AI’s existential and societal risks remain serious questions. Packaging and isolation can reduce particular operational risks; they do not guarantee that AI cannot behave dangerously or that humans will always use it well. Honest limits are part of care.

workflow.title: Prepare a real workspace
workflow.text: Choose a Git repository with a valid HEAD and define the work that may happen. Decide which data and credentials each service needs.

workflow.title: Build and verify the baseline
workflow.text: Check the Nix recipe, build the OCI image and run the documented container verification. Keep the image pin and evidence.

workflow.title: Connect the right tools
workflow.text: Use Sylvae for portable execution, WeftMark for evidence and review, and Nostoi for audit integrity. Expose only the gateway routes the deployment needs.

workflow.title: Make oversight explicit
workflow.text: Enable Ephor only when you deliberately want its governance integration. Keep human decisions authenticated and separate from the agents’ working credentials.

quickstart.title: Build the public baseline
quickstart.summary: Start from the repository with Nix flakes and a Docker-compatible runtime. Read the deployment contract before exposing a service or mounting a workspace.
quickstart.note: The commands below build and load an image. A secure runtime configuration, persistent state, a valid Git workspace and a deliberate image pin are still required.

commands.label: Check and build
commands.code:
git clone https://github.com/tabenius/rebekah.git
cd rebekah
nix flake check
nix build .#image
docker load < result

pages.title: Give the runtime boundaries you can explain
pages.description: A short checklist for separating a public website, an authenticated gateway and the self-hosted workshop.

sections.title: Build from known source
paragraphs: Use the canonical deployment contract and pinned inputs. Record the image digest or image ID you actually intend to run.
The public baseline is independent of Ephor. Opt-in governance has a separate build and source-access requirement.

sections.title: Give each service its own responsibility
paragraphs: Keep service state and credentials separate. Put remote clients through the authenticated gateway and expose only the required backend routes.
Do not move an agent’s working credentials into a review authority’s environment merely because both belong to the same container.

sections.title: Verify the actual deployment
paragraphs: Exercise the real container, restart behaviour and isolation boundaries. A project website’s health endpoint only certifies the website.
Then use WeftMark for the engineering evidence, Sylvae for deliberate execution and Nostoi for chain integrity where relevant. Bring questions and judgments back to people.
